record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Singularities of Mappings
record.original_question: For a stable perturbation f_t: U -> C^(n+1) of an A_e-codimension-one mono-germ f: (C^n,0) -> (C^(n+1),0), the image-computing filtration expresses the image vanishing homology through alternating homology of the multiple-point spaces D_k(f_t). Which multiple-point space D_k(f_t) carries the single alternating vanishing cycle that gives rise to the vanishing cycle in the image or discriminant?

evidence.quote: just one of the multiple point spaces of ft or ft|Sigma ft has an alternating vanishing cycle
Question 2.2. (i) In the case of a stable perturbation of a Ae-codimension 1 mono-germ, how to determine which multiple-point space carries the vanishing alternating cycle?

artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of identifying which multiple-point space carries the alternating vanishing cycle for a stable perturbation of an A_e-codimension-one mono-germ appears to remain open. Partial results are known: for minimal corank-1 codimension-one map-germs f:(C^{2m-1},0)→(C^{2m},0), the alternating vanishing cycle is known to live in H_m(D_{m+1}(f_t)); related results by Cooper–Mond–Houston (Compositio Math.) describe alternating vanishing homology in codimension-1 multi-germs, but no uniform answer covering all corank and dimension cases has been published.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f:(C^n,0)→(C^{n+1},0) be a holomorphic mono-germ that is finite, generically one-to-one, and of A_e-codimension one (so the base of a miniversal unfolding of f modulo A-equivalence is one-dimensional). For a generic small parameter t, let f_t:U→C^{n+1} be a stable perturbation of f defined on a small representative U⊂C^n. For each integer k≥1, the k-th multiple-point space of f_t is

  D_k(f_t) = closure{(x_1,…,x_k) ∈ U^k : x_i ≠ x_j for i≠j, f_t(x_1)=…=f_t(x_k)},

equipped with the natural action of the symmetric group S_k by permutation of coordinates. Denote by H_*^{Alt}(D_k(f_t);Q) the alternating part of its rational homology under this S_k-action, i.e. the subspace on which σ∈S_k acts by sign(σ).

It is known that there is a spectral sequence with E_1-page consisting of the groups H_*^{Alt}(D_k(f_t);Q) that converges to the (reduced) homology of the image of f_t, and that for an A_e-codimension-one mono-germ the total vanishing homology of the image (or of the discriminant, in the case where f_t lifts via a stable map) is concentrated in a single rank-one summand corresponding to a single alternating vanishing cycle living in exactly one of the multiple-point spaces.

Problem. Give an effective rule that, from the data of the germ f (e.g. its corank, source dimension n, and normal form), determines the integer k=k(f) such that the alternating vanishing cycle lies in H_*^{Alt}(D_k(f_t);Q), and identify the homological degree in which it occurs.
